title: Briefing: Italy's student and cost-of-living protests, Albania's student protests and France's high school protests
script: This is the Unowned briefing for Sunday, October twenty-fifth. It's narrated by a synthetic voice, and every fact comes from our checked timelines.

Italy holds a fourth round of nationwide protests called by Movimento 17 Ottobre, with marches or rallies reported in at least ten cities including Rome, Milan, Turin and Bologna, Euronews and Il Sole 24 Ore report. That's confirmed by independent reports. What's next: a reconciled national total of arrests, detentions and injuries from the October twenty-fourth protests.

Democratic Party supporters gather outside the prime minister's office and set fire to pillows Rama had placed there as a symbolic invitation to dialogue, before moving to join the student protest at the Education Ministry. That's confirmed by independent reports. What's next: a reconciled arrest and injury total for Saturday's rally.

The interior ministry says 410,000 people protested nationwide on Saturday, including 110,000 in Paris, in marches over the cost of living and the high-school movement; the CGT union puts both figures at nearly double the official count. That's reported so far by one source. We're watching whether Monday's government meeting produces concrete decisions on staffing.
That's the briefing. Full timelines, and every source, are at unowned news dot com.
